review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Humidity, wind and rotational measurement; acceleration action/quantity distinction; dimensional tools, timekeeping and selected inherited terminology.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Normalized lemma candidates only; Russian labels and concept context still require review.

review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet. CC BY 4.0 and the underlying Princeton notice are retained in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. Russian labels, sense restrictions, productive action phrases, and graph mappings are adaptations.
review.context_policy: All new concepts and assertions use U1. Existing home contexts remain unchanged; change 2606 also receives its missing U1 parent without removing its U5 parent. U2 stays empty.

sense_decisions.scope: Wetness is broader than atmospheric humidity.
Existing damp property receives a real English translation.
Existing wet property receives a real English translation.
Moisture in atmospheric air, narrower than the existing wetness property.
Humidity expressed relative to saturation at the same temperature. It is distinct from mass of water per volume of air.
Mass of water vapour per volume of air; distinct from relative and specific humidity.
The temperature at which air becomes saturated upon cooling under the specified pressure and moisture conditions. It is a temperature, not a geometrical point or a humidity percentage.
Measurement of atmospheric humidity.
Measurement specifically of relative humidity.
An instrument for measuring humidity; retain the broader NWS usage rather than require every hygrometer to report relative humidity.
The paired wet/dry-bulb instrument determines humidity from two temperature readings.
The dry-bulb thermometer used as the ambient-temperature reference; distinct from the temperature reading.
The thermometer with a moistened covering at its bulb; distinct from a generic thermometer merely exposed to wet weather.
The speed of air motion, distinct from the direction from which the wind blows.
The rate of repeated cycles of a periodic process; exclude statistical relative frequency and an absolute category count. Oscillation frequency is a narrower application, not an imported synonym.
Number of revolutions per unit time, as reported by a tachometer. Do not equate it with angular velocity in radians per second.
A rotational-frequency unit, not the rotational-frequency property itself. The r/min notation is supported by the instrument manual.
Rate of change of velocity, including direction changes and slowing down. The dictionary increase-only gloss is too narrow.
Measurement of scalar speed.
The speed measurement made with an anemometer. No wind-direction capability is universally asserted.
Measurement of periodic frequency, distinct from counting statistical category membership.
Measurement of revolutions per unit time.
Measurement of acceleration; no universal zero-at-rest or gravity-compensation behaviour is asserted.
Use the NWS wind-speed function. Direction measurement is not required of every anemometer.
An instrument indicating vehicle speed; not distance travelled.
An instrument measuring rotational rate; do not use general linear speed as its selected target.
A sensor for measuring acceleration, not limited to aircraft or rockets as in the dictionary example.
An instrument intended for linear-dimension measurement. This includes rulers, tapes, micrometers and calipers.
Restrict the broad dictionary caliper to the sliding-jaw instrument denoted by the Russian term. Micrometers are not classified as sliding calipers.
The sliding caliper with a vernier scale. The ambiguous vernier micrometer synonym is excluded.
The sliding caliper with a dial indication; its display differs from a vernier scale.
The sliding caliper with a digital indication; no universal accuracy or material is asserted.
The length of the diameter segment, distinct from that geometric segment itself.
Measurement of the diameter length, not measurement of an abstract line as an object.
Measurement of depth, a reviewed existing length concept.
An instrument for the depth of holes, grooves or other recesses; not a gauge of an arbitrary numerical quantity.
The process of determining time, specializing measurement. The existing generic counting-out verbs are not synonyms.
The shared instrument class for clocks, interval timers and stopwatches. It is not a person acting as a timekeeper.
The timer that measures an interval and signals its end; not the control-switch device or sports official.
Preserve the existing time-of-day clock identity under the new shared timepiece family.
The stopwatch retains its existing duration-measurement purpose.
The level using a bubble vial. Manufacturer examples also support vertical readings; not every level is restricted to horizontal use.
Reuse ruler, preserving its tool classification and measurement purpose.
Reuse tape measure and its purpose.
Reuse micrometer instrument, separate from the length unit and sliding caliper.
Reuse the thermometer as genus of wet/dry-bulb instruments.
Reuse depth as a length quantity.
Reuse scalar speed.
Reuse rotation as a motion process.
Reuse wind as a phenomenon.
Generic counting-out action with malformed aliases; not exact timekeeping. Separate lexical review pending.
Possible counting-out duplicate; no merge without reviewing its lexical history.
Spatial-direction taxonomy and action aliases need review before wind-direction measurement.
Horizontal orientation is misclassified as shape; defer the orientation cohort.
Mixed habitual/typical/frequent children remain pending after removing only the invalid time genus.
The English caliper umbrella spans more tools than Russian shtangentsirkul. No broad Russian equivalence or micrometer-to-sliding-caliper edge is asserted.

review.limits: This cohort is not a bulk synset import. General caliper is broader than Russian shtangentsirkul; only the sliding-caliper sense and supported subtypes are added. Vernier scales, geometric segment/chord genera, wetness-value duplicates, other frequency/duration children, wind direction, and the wider counting duplicates remain pending. Numerical conversions and sensor operating conditions are not encoded as genus or attribute links. No automatic confidence percentages or application test suites.

collision_decisions.decision: Keep separate qualified quantity and speeding-up process concepts. The shared Russian acceleration term is intentionally ambiguous for lookup.
Keep separate qualified length and geometric-segment concepts. Both retain bare diameter terms; lexical identity is not sense identity.

review.superseded_q11_conditions: Q11 direct genus conditions for ruler 1501, tape measure 2338, micrometer instrument 24572, and stopwatch 24570 are superseded by nearer genera. Their previous broader genera remain ancestors; their Q11 purpose edges are preserved.
